History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
30-year-old female nurse with 7-day history of persistent fever, alternating chills/sweats, myalgias, nausea, and fatigue one month after rural travel in Vietnam; no localizing symptoms, prompting in-person exam and urgent labs (including malaria films) to identify infectious etiology.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Persistent daily fever with drenching sweats and feeling “hot and sweaty all the time” for 7 days.  
• Timeline: Onset ~7 days ago; symptoms unchanged despite OTC antipyretics. Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago.  
• Symptom progression: Ongoing; no clear improvement.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Generalized myalgias/“aching all over.”  
  – Nausea with poor oral intake.  
  – Marked fatigue; night sweats; alternating chills and feeling cold.  
• Denied symptoms: Cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, new/worsening headache, rash, swollen joints, dysuria, urinary frequency/urgency.  
• Exacerbating/Relieving factors: Paracetamol and ibuprofen give slight, temporary fever relief.  
• Review of systems: Otherwise non-contributory per transcript.

Past Medical History:
• Chronic mechanical/positional back pain – under physiotherapy care; no surgical history noted.  
• Episodic tension/migraine headaches related to screen use and weather changes (long-standing).  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• Seroxat (paroxetine) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Ibuprofen – OTC, recommended dose, exact regimen not documented.  
• Paracetamol – OTC, recommended dose, exact regimen not documented.  
• Completed daily malaria prophylaxis in Vietnam (drug name not recalled).

Allergies:
• Pollen (hay fever).  
• No medication allergies reported.

Social History:
• Occupation: Nurse; currently struggling at work due to fatigue.  
• Smoking: Never.  
• Alcohol: Moderate intake (quantities not specified).  
• Exercise: Moderate physical activity several times per week.  
• Travel: Three-week trip to Vietnam; trekking, cycling, rural/river exposure; returned 4 weeks ago.  
• Vaccinations: Up to date, including Hepatitis B.

Family History:
• Father died of myocardial infarction at age 68.  
• No other familial conditions reported.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed in teleconsult; patient to be examined in clinic.)

Investigations:
• None to date.  
• Planned: Thick & thin blood films for malaria; full blood count; inflammatory markers (e.g., CRP/ESR); additional labs per in-person assessment.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Febrile illness of uncertain origin, post-travel:  
  • Assessment: 7-day fever with night sweats, myalgias, nausea; no focal source on ROS; returned from malaria-endemic area 4 weeks ago.  
  • Plan:  
    – Urgent in-person examination today at central London clinic (or local A&E if preferred).  
    – Blood tests: malaria thick/thin smears, FBC, inflammatory markers; consider liver/renal profile and blood cultures based on exam.  
    – Advise patient not to work until evaluated.  
    – Provide written note/request for tests to reception on arrival.

Issue 2 – Possible travel-related infection (malaria highest on DDx; consider dengue, typhoid, other tropical infections):  
  • Plan:  
    – Detailed travel history including prophylaxis adherence and exact drug once in clinic.  
    – Additional studies as guided by exam/labs (e.g., dengue serology, blood cultures for Salmonella Typhi, viral PCR).  
    – Initiate empiric therapy only if clinically indicated after evaluation.

Issue 3 – Chronic mechanical back pain:  
  • Stable; continue physiotherapy and posture exercises. No change in current management required during acute work-up.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Malaria – High likelihood: Recent rural Vietnam travel, alternating chills/sweats, fever, myalgias; prophylaxis not fully protective and drug adherence/efficacy uncertain.  
2. Acute systemic viral infection (e.g., influenza/COVID-19) – Moderate likelihood: Constitutional viral symptoms without focal signs; however, 7-day persistent high fever less typical.  
3. Dengue or other arboviral illness – Low-moderate likelihood: Endemic exposure and systemic symptoms; onset 4 weeks post-travel is later than usual and no rash or retro-orbital pain reported.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Objective vitals, physical-exam findings, complete medication list with doses, allergy reconciliation for drugs/foods/latex, pregnancy status (relevant in febrile female of child-bearing age), COVID-19 testing status.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None identified.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational pauses but information comprehensible.
